front: What should you do before drawing components in a system-design interview?
back: Clarify the core user flows, correctness requirements, scale, latency, availability, consistency, security, and explicit non-goals so the architecture solves the right problem.
accepted_answers: Clarify the core user flows, correctness requirements, scale, latency, availability, consistency, security, and explicit non-goals so the architecture solves the right problem.
hint: Requirements and constraints come before boxes and arrows.

front: Why make rough traffic and storage estimates in system design?
back: Back-of-the-envelope estimates reveal the order of magnitude for throughput, bandwidth, storage, and hot paths, which determines whether simple designs are sufficient or partitioning and caching are justified.
accepted_answers: Back-of-the-envelope estimates reveal the order of magnitude for throughput, bandwidth, storage, and hot paths, which determines whether simple designs are sufficient or partitioning and caching are justified.
hint: Estimate to choose architecture, not to impress with arithmetic.

front: What is the main role of a load balancer?
back: It distributes incoming work across healthy service instances and can provide health-based routing, connection management, and a stable entry point while instances scale or fail.
accepted_answers: It distributes incoming work across healthy service instances and can provide health-based routing, connection management, and a stable entry point while instances scale or fail.
hint: Decouple clients from individual backend instances.

front: Why are stateless application instances easier to scale horizontally?
back: Any request can be routed to any healthy instance because durable session or business state lives in shared systems, reducing affinity constraints and making replacement and autoscaling simpler.
accepted_answers: Any request can be routed to any healthy instance because durable session or business state lives in shared systems, reducing affinity constraints and making replacement and autoscaling simpler.
hint: Keep replaceable compute separate from durable state.

front: What trade-off do read replicas introduce?
back: They can scale read throughput and isolate read traffic, but replication lag means replicas may serve stale data and they add failover, routing, and consistency complexity.
accepted_answers: They can scale read throughput and isolate read traffic, but replication lag means replicas may serve stale data and they add failover, routing, and consistency complexity.
hint: More read capacity can mean weaker read-after-write behavior.

front: What makes a good partition key?
back: It spreads load and storage reasonably evenly, supports the dominant access patterns without excessive cross-partition work, and avoids predictable hot keys.
accepted_answers: It spreads load and storage reasonably evenly, supports the dominant access patterns without excessive cross-partition work, and avoids predictable hot keys.
hint: Balance distribution with query locality.

front: What is a hot partition?
back: A hot partition receives disproportionate traffic or data because many requests map to the same partition key or range, so one shard becomes the bottleneck while others remain underused.
accepted_answers: A hot partition receives disproportionate traffic or data because many requests map to the same partition key or range, so one shard becomes the bottleneck while others remain underused.
hint: Uniform shard count does not guarantee uniform load.

front: When is cache-aside appropriate?
back: The application reads the cache first, loads from the source on a miss, and populates the cache; it is simple and effective for read-heavy data when stale-data and invalidation behavior are acceptable.
accepted_answers: The application reads the cache first, loads from the source on a miss, and populates the cache; it is simple and effective for read-heavy data when stale-data and invalidation behavior are acceptable.
hint: Application-managed lazy population.

front: What causes a cache stampede and how can you reduce it?
back: Many requests miss or expire the same hot key simultaneously and all hit the backing store; mitigate with request coalescing, jittered TTLs, stale-while-revalidate, or controlled locking.
accepted_answers: Many requests miss or expire the same hot key simultaneously and all hit the backing store; mitigate with request coalescing, jittered TTLs, stale-while-revalidate, or controlled locking.
hint: One hot expiration can synchronize thousands of callers.

front: How does a token-bucket rate limiter behave?
back: Tokens accumulate up to a capacity at a fixed rate, requests spend tokens, and bursts are allowed while tokens exist; sustained traffic is limited by the refill rate.
accepted_answers: Tokens accumulate up to a capacity at a fixed rate, requests spend tokens, and bursts are allowed while tokens exist; sustained traffic is limited by the refill rate.
hint: It permits bounded bursts while enforcing a long-term rate.

front: Why introduce an asynchronous queue between services?
back: A queue can absorb bursts, decouple producer latency from consumer work, enable retries, and provide backpressure, but it introduces delivery semantics, ordering, lag, and operational complexity.
accepted_answers: A queue can absorb bursts, decouple producer latency from consumer work, enable retries, and provide backpressure, but it introduces delivery semantics, ordering, lag, and operational complexity.
hint: Decoupling buys resilience at the cost of asynchronous behavior.

front: Why should retryable APIs be idempotent?
back: Clients and intermediaries cannot always know whether a timed-out request committed, so retrying must not create duplicate business effects; use stable operation identity and durable deduplication where needed.
accepted_answers: Clients and intermediaries cannot always know whether a timed-out request committed, so retrying must not create duplicate business effects; use stable operation identity and durable deduplication where needed.
hint: A timeout is ambiguous, not proof of failure.

front: What problem does a circuit breaker solve?
back: It temporarily stops sending normal traffic to a dependency that is repeatedly failing, reducing wasted work and allowing recovery instead of amplifying a cascading failure.
accepted_answers: It temporarily stops sending normal traffic to a dependency that is repeatedly failing, reducing wasted work and allowing recovery instead of amplifying a cascading failure.
hint: Fail fast after evidence that a dependency is unhealthy.

front: What is the purpose of a bulkhead?
back: A bulkhead partitions scarce resources such as thread pools, connections, or concurrency slots so one dependency or workload cannot exhaust capacity needed by unrelated traffic.
accepted_answers: A bulkhead partitions scarce resources such as thread pools, connections, or concurrency slots so one dependency or workload cannot exhaust capacity needed by unrelated traffic.
hint: Failure isolation through resource boundaries.

front: Why does multi-region active-active architecture increase complexity?
back: Writes can occur in multiple locations, so conflict resolution, global consistency, routing, replication lag, data residency, and split-brain behavior all become explicit design problems.
accepted_answers: Writes can occur in multiple locations, so conflict resolution, global consistency, routing, replication lag, data residency, and split-brain behavior all become explicit design problems.
hint: Geographic redundancy changes consistency and coordination.

front: How should a system-design answer choose between strong and eventual consistency?
back: Tie the choice to business invariants: use stronger coordination where stale or conflicting state can violate correctness, and allow eventual consistency where temporary divergence is acceptable for availability or scale.
accepted_answers: Tie the choice to business invariants: use stronger coordination where stale or conflicting state can violate correctness, and allow eventual consistency where temporary divergence is acceptable for availability or scale.
hint: Consistency is a product requirement, not a universal maximum.

front: Why should the data model be discussed early in system design?
back: Access patterns, transaction boundaries, cardinality, uniqueness, and retention shape storage and partitioning choices; a vague database box hides many of the system's hardest correctness decisions.
accepted_answers: Access patterns, transaction boundaries, cardinality, uniqueness, and retention shape storage and partitioning choices; a vague database box hides many of the system's hardest correctness decisions.
hint: Model the reads, writes, and invariants, not just components.

front: What observability should a design include before production?
back: Define service-level metrics, structured logs, distributed traces where valuable, correlation identifiers, dashboards, alerts tied to user impact, and enough diagnostic context to distinguish dependency and capacity failures.
accepted_answers: Define service-level metrics, structured logs, distributed traces where valuable, correlation identifiers, dashboards, alerts tied to user impact, and enough diagnostic context to distinguish dependency and capacity failures.
hint: Operability is part of the architecture.

front: What is graceful degradation?
back: When a noncritical dependency fails or capacity is constrained, the system intentionally serves a reduced but useful experience rather than failing the entire request path.
accepted_answers: When a noncritical dependency fails or capacity is constrained, the system intentionally serves a reduced but useful experience rather than failing the entire request path.
hint: Preserve core value while shedding optional behavior.

front: Why are tail latencies important in distributed systems?
back: A request that fans out to many dependencies is often gated by its slowest calls, so p95 and p99 behavior can dominate user latency even when average latency looks healthy.
accepted_answers: A request that fans out to many dependencies is often gated by its slowest calls, so p95 and p99 behavior can dominate user latency even when average latency looks healthy.
hint: Fan-out magnifies slow outliers.
